releases.title: DiRT 3 — TU and unlocked FPS game-folder files
releases.notes:
DiRT 3 original-release TU and FPS files for a complete extracted game folder launched through Neighborhood.

Title ID: `434D083D` · Media ID: `75036F79` · Executable version: `0.0.1.3`.

### Assets

- `Dirt3_TU_clean_gamefolder_control.xex`: TU merged and local update-data lookup; no FPS edits.
- `Dirt3_TU_unlocked_gamefolder.xex`: the same baseline with both published FPS edits.
- `patch.nfs`: unchanged matching TU data, required beside the XEX.
- `Dirt3_TU_gamefolder_test.zip`: both XEXs, update data, instructions and verification record.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt`: checksums for the individual files.

Both candidates redirect the update-data filesystem prefix from `update:` to `game:`. Copy both XEXs and `patch.nfs` beside the untouched original `default.xex` in the complete extracted game folder. Launch the control through Neighborhood first, then the unlocked version if the control loads.

### Console feedback and reproduction

The contributor reports that the original-release unlocked XEX works on the RGH console. The earlier TU-unlocked file showed “This disc is unreadable” through Neighborhood. These game-folder variants add the local update-data path revision; no further console result has been recorded for their exact hashes. This is not a claim that the original error has been resolved.

The earlier failing XEX was independently reproduced byte for byte from the uploaded original, TU and guide edits. Both long signatures matched once. The new candidates passed exact dumped-payload checks. All 25 compressed blocks in patch.nfs matched their stored checksums; its build number matches the executable.

For GOD conversion after extracted-folder testing, use ISO2GOD Next's XEX-folder input directly. Older ISO2GOD versions can use an ISO rebuilt from the complete modified game folder. See the repository README for both methods.

ZIP SHA-256: `1365bf498c3bbed5be6475481fc60dce79688abce26e74d8d29395713d6d06b6`.

releases.title: Rainbow Six Vegas 2 — unlocked FPS and V-sync files
releases.notes:
# Rainbow Six Vegas 2 — unlocked framerate and vsync variants

For **RGH/JTAG Xbox 360 consoles**, title ID **55530807**, media ID **1982EE1E**. These XEX files are not re-signed.

Download one of the three separate assets in this release:

| Asset | Build | Presentation behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RSV2_base_unlocked.xex | Base v00000001 | Unlocked presentation; tearing can occur |
| RSV2_TU_unlocked.xex | Matching TU executable merged, v00000201 | Unlocked presentation; tearing can occur |
| RSV2_TU_vsync60.xex | Matching TU executable merged, v00000201 | One-refresh vsync interval; a 60 FPS presentation ceiling on a 60 Hz display |

The user reports that unlocked RSV2 runs with the title update and benefits in smaller Terrorist Hunt maps. The user also reports that vsync reduces tearing. These observations do not establish a measured or sustained 60 FPS result, and the exact tested file hashes were not recorded.

Back up your original `default.xex`. Choose the asset matching your game/update setup, rename it to `default.xex`, and place it in the game folder. Keep the matching game/update installation: the TU assets include the merged executable changes, preserve `UPDATE:` paths, and are not a complete update package.

All three assets match the previously verified files byte for byte. Their only changes from the clean normalized or TU-merged executable are the documented presentation instructions.

releases.title: Bully: Scholarship Edition — unlocked FPS and V-sync files
releases.notes:
# Bully: Scholarship Edition — Xbox 360 FPS variants

Modified XEX files for an RGH/JTAG Xbox 360, for title `5454081A`, media
`0867AD86` (North America). Console testing is reported by the user; FPS was not
independently benchmarked in the file audit.

| Download | Build | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bully_base_unlocked.xex` | Base v1 (`00000001`) | Vsync off; unlocked presentation with possible tearing |
| `Bully_TU_unlocked.xex` | Updated v0.0.1.1 (`00000101`) | Vsync off; unlocked presentation with possible tearing |
| `Bully_TU_vsync60.xex` | Updated v0.0.1.1 (`00000101`) | Interval 1, intended for vsync at 60 Hz |

Choose one matching your game build. Back up `default.xex`, copy the chosen file
into the game folder, and rename it to `default.xex`. Keep the backup to restore
the original. The updated executables are supplied as complete files; their
historical provenance records matching TU package
`TU_1A5820Q_0000004000000.0000000000081` merged into the executable. Do not assume
compatibility with a different media ID or layer an unrelated TU over them.

These patches change frame presentation behavior. Actual FPS depends on the
game's workload; “vsync60” does not promise a steady 60 FPS.

The audit verified the supplied asset hashes, title/media/version metadata and
native images. The updated unlocked/vsync files have identical headers and differ
by exactly five bytes: the interval-load instruction and the unlock mask byte.
The archive did not include an original executable or TU package, so its original
patching and update merge were not independently reproduced.
